titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Translator's Colophon and the List of Kings (Colophon)
part: Colophon — The Translator's Colophon and the List of Kings
about: The colophon of the book: how it was brought out of Arabic into Geʿez, the translator Isaac's plea for prayers, and a closing list of the kings of Ethiopia from the Aksumite brothers to Amda Seyon.

sentences.t: ወተብህለ ፡ በክታበ ፡ ዐረቢ ፡ አውፃእናሃ ፡ እመጽሐፈ ፡ ቅብጥ ፡ ለዐረቢ ፡ እመንበረ ፡ ማርቆስ ፡ ወንጌላዊ ፡ መምህር ፡ አበ ፡ ኵልነ ፤
sentences.l: And-it-was-said: in-writing-of Arabic we-brought-it-out it, from-book-of Copts to-Arabic, from-throne-of Mark evangelist teacher father-of all-of-us;
sentences.i: It is said: we brought it out in an Arabic writing, from the book of the Copts into Arabic, from the see of Mark the evangelist, the teacher, the father of us all;
sentences.n: Colophon: a new voice, a translator's first person plural. ወ- 'and' + ተብህለ 'it was said' (passive, Gt-type stem of በሀለ). አውፃእናሃ is አውፅአ 'bring out' with 1cp ending -ነ and 3fs object -ሃ 'it' (the book, ጽሐፍ fem.); 'bring out' is the usual word for publishing or rendering a text. እም- 'from' also on እመጽሐፈ, እመንበረ. The Copts = the Egyptian church; the throne (መንበር) of Mark is the see of Alexandria. አበ ኵልነ 'father of all of us': ኵሉ + -ነ.

sentences.t: ወአውፃእናሃ ፡ በ፬፻ ፡ ወ፱ ፡ ዓመተ ፡ ምሕረት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ በመዋዕለ ፡ ገብረ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወሰጓሁ ፡ ላሊበላ ፡ በመዋዕለ ፡ አባ ፡ ጊዮርጊስ ፡ ጳጳስ ፡ ኄር ፡ ወአስተተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አውፅኦታ ፡ ወተርጒሞታ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ነገረ ፡ ሐባሲ ፡ ወሶበ ፡ ኀለይኩ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ለምንት ፡ ኢተርጐምዋ ፡ አበልዕዝ ፡ ወአበልፈረግ ፡ እለ ፡ አውፅእዋ ፡ እቤ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ እስመ ፡ ወፅአት ፡ በመዋዕለ ፡ ዛጓ ፡ ወኢተርጐምዋ ፡ እስመ ፡ ትብል ፡ ዛቲ ፡ መጽሐፍ ፡ እለሰ ፡ ይነግሡ ፡ እለ ፡ ኢኮኑ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ተዐድዎ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-we-brought-it-out in-4 hundred and-9 year-of mercy, in land-of Ethiopia, in-days-of Gebre Mesqel king, and-(?) Lalibela; in-days-of Abba Giyorgis bishop good; and-God completed (?) its-bringing-out and-its-translation to speech-of Abyssinian; and-when I-considered this, why not-they-translated-it Abelʿəz and-Abelfäräg who they-brought-it-out — I-said this: because it-came-out in-days-of Zagwe, and-they-did-not-translate-it; because says this book: those-who they-reign who not-are Israel, transgression-of law it-is;
sentences.i: And we brought it out in the four hundred and ninth year of mercy, in the land of Ethiopia, in the days of King Gebre Mesqel and Lalibela (?), in the days of Abba Giyorgis, the good bishop; and God completed (?) its bringing out and its translation into the speech of the Abyssinians. And when I considered this — why did they not translate it, the Abelʿəz and the Abelfäräg (?) who brought it out — I said: it is because it came out in the days of the Zagwe, and they did not translate it; for this book says that those who reign who are not Israel are transgressing the law (?).
sentences.n: A long unit (54 words), kept whole; the source has no ፤ in it. 'Year of mercy' (ዓመተ ምሕረት) is the Ethiopian era, so ፬፻ወ፱ is 409 (here in the Ethiopian reckoning, about the early 1300s CE — the date is the colophon's, not ours to settle). Gebre Mesqel is the regnal name of Lalibela; ወሰጓሁ ላሊበላ is obscure (?): ሰጓሁ could be a verb with 3ms suffix 'and … him' — left unresolved and rendered as a bare apposition. ወአስተተ 'completed' is a hedged reading (?) from ተተ. ሐባሲ 'Abyssinian'. አበልዕዝ and አበልፈረግ are not securely analysed (?): they may be personal names or a pair of descriptions; they follow እለ አውፅእዋ 'who brought it out' and so name the earlier translators. ዛጓ is the Zagwe dynasty. ኢተርጐምዋ: negated ተርጐመ 'translate' with 3mp -ዋ 'it'. እስመ ትብል: 'for … says' with the book (fem.) as subject. ተዐድዎ ሕግ 'transgression of law': the last words are hard (?) — read as ተዐድዎ 'transgression' + ሕግ + ውእቱ 'it is'.

sentences.i: And when it comes to be in the kingdom of Israel (?), from [the time] they brought it out;
sentences.n: Obscure (?): the clause is cut short. ሶበ 'when' + ይከውን 'it will be'; እምአውፅእዋ is እም- 'from' + አውፅእዋ 'they brought it out' (3mp + 3fs), so 'from their bringing it out'. The sense — presumably that the book, once in the kingdom of the Israelite line, was found in Nazareth — is not certain.

sentences.i: And it was found in Nazareth.
sentences.n: ወተረክበት 'and it was found' (ተረክበ, passive of ረከበ, 3fs). Nazareth here is a place-name; its identity in this colophon is not explained (?). ፨ marks a paragraph-end.

sentences.t: ወጸልዩ ፡ ላዕሌየ ፡ ለገብርክሙ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ነዳይ ፡ ወኢትሒሱኒ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ኢያርትዖ ፡ ነገረ ፡ ልሳን ፤
sentences.l: And-pray upon-me for-your-servant Isaac poor, and-not-blame-me for not-straightening-of speech-of language;
sentences.i: And pray for me, for your servant Isaac, the poor man, and do not blame me for any lack of correctness in the speech of the language;
sentences.n: Isaac is the translator, speaking in his own voice. ወጸልዩ is ጸለየ 'pray' in the plural imperative; ላዕሌየ 'upon me' (ላዕለ + -የ). ለገብርክሙ: ለ- + ገብር 'servant' + -ክሙ 'your (mp)'. ወኢትሒሱኒ: ኢ- + ትሒሱ 'you (pl.) blame' (ሐሰ, here 'reproach', hedged) + -ኒ 'me'. ኢያርትዖ is a verbal noun with negative — 'not setting straight' (አርትዐ 'make straight').

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ ጻመውኩ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ክብራ ፡ ለሀገረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጸአታ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ወበእንተ ፡ ክብረ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ እስመ ፡ አነሂ ፡ ተስእልክዎ ፡ ለመኰንን ፡ ርቱዕ ፡ ፍቁረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ያዕቢከ ፡ እግዚእ ፡ ወአፍቀረ ፡ ወይቤለኒ ፡ ግበር ፤
sentences.l: For much I-laboured for-glory-of-her of-land-of Ethiopia, for-the-going-out-of-her of-Zion heavenly, and-for glory-of king-of Ethiopia; for I-also I-asked-him the-governor just, beloved-of God: 'Makes-great-you Lord and-he-loved'; and-he-said-to-me: 'Do';
sentences.i: For I laboured much for the glory of the land of Ethiopia, for the going out of heavenly Zion, and for the glory of the king of Ethiopia; for I too asked the just governor, the beloved of God, 'May the Lord make you great' (?) — and he loved it (?), and he said to me, 'Do it';
sentences.n: እስመ 'for' opens the reason. ብዙኀ is an adverbial accusative 'much'. በእንተ ክብራ ለሀገረ ኢትዮጵያ is 'for her glory, of the land': a possessive suffix anticipates the owner, introduced by ለ-; so also ጸአታ ለጽዮን. The 'going out' of Zion is the Ark's going out (to Ethiopia), the theme of the whole book; ሰማያዊት 'heavenly' is feminine to agree with ጽዮን. መኰንን 'governor, judge' and ፍቁረ እግዚኣብሔር 'beloved of God' (construct) are in apposition; whom this is is not said. The words between are unclear (?): ያዕቢከ 'makes you great / may he make you great' (3ms + -ከ) and ወአፍቀረ 'and he loved' — a greeting, or a speech whose frame is lost. ተስእልክዎ: 1cs perfect 'I asked' + 3ms object.

sentences.t: ወገበርኩ ፡ እንዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይረድአኒ ፡ ወኢፈደየኒ ፡ በከመ ፡ አበሳየ ፡ ለገብርክሙ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ጸልዩ ፡ ወለእለ ፡ ፃመዉ ፡ ምስሌየ ፡ በፀአተ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ መጽሐፍ ፡ እስመ ፡ ተመንደብነ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ አነ ፡ ወይምሀረነ ፡ አብ ፡ ወሕዝበ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ወእንድርያስ ፡ ወፊልጶስ ፡ ወመሓሪ ፡ አብ ፡ ይምሐሮሙ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ በመንግሥተ ፡ ሰማያት ፡ ምስለ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ቅዱሳን ፡ ወሰማዕት ፡ ይጽሐፍ ፡ ስሞሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መጽሐፈ ፡ ሕይወት ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፡ ወአሜን ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-I-did while God helps-me, and-not-he-repaid-me according-to my-fault; pray for-your-servant Isaac, and-for-those who they-laboured with-me in-going-out-of this book, for we-were-distressed (?) exceedingly, I; and-may-have-mercy-on-us Father and-people-of Christ and-Andrew and-Philip and-merciful Father; may-have-mercy-on-them God in-kingdom-of heavens with all-of-them saints and-martyrs; may-be-written their-names in book-of life for ever-of ever, amen and-amen.
sentences.i: And I did it, while God helped me, and he did not repay me according to my fault. Pray for your servant Isaac, and for those who laboured with me in the going out of this book, for we were greatly distressed (?), I [above all]. May the Father have mercy on us, and the people of Christ, and Andrew and Philip, and the merciful Father; may God have mercy on them in the kingdom of heaven with all the saints and martyrs; may their names be written in the book of life, for ever and ever. Amen and amen.
sentences.n: A long unit (45 words); the closing ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ is a row of end-marks. እንዘ 'while' + the imperfect ይረድአኒ 'he helps me' (ረድአ + -ኒ). ወኢፈደየኒ: ፈደየ 'repay' + -ኒ. ተመንደብነ is not secure (?): a passive stem with 1cp ending, 'we were distressed' (from መንደበ). ፈድፋደ 'exceedingly'. ወይምሀረነ and ይምሐሮሙ are jussives of መሐረ 'have mercy' (ሀ for ሐ in the first is the text's spelling; ምህረ 'teach' is the other possible root — read here as 'have mercy' to match the parallel clause (?)). The persons named — the Father, the people of Christ, Andrew, Philip, 'the merciful Father' — are as the text lists them; the identification of the last is not given (?). 'Book of life' recalls Philippians 4:3 and Revelation 3:5 (ጽሐፈ ሕይወት 'book of life'). ለዓለመ ዓለም 'for ever and ever'; ኵሎሙ 'all of them' (ኵሉ + -ሙ).

sentences.i: And after the birth of our Saviour, these are the kings:
sentences.n: A new section: a list of the kings who reigned. እምድኅረ 'after' + ተወልደ 'was born' (passive of ወለደ), subject መድኀኒነ 'our Saviour' (መድኀኒ + -ነ). እሉ is the plural 'these', ነገሥት 'kings' (broken plural of ንጉሥ). Every unit that follows is one king's name, ending at ፤; the list ends at ፨. The Geʿez spellings are kept exactly; the English forms are conventional ones, and the names have no certain sense unless a note says so.
King's name; the sense, if any, is not claimed.
Name: ጽንፈ may be ጽንፍ 'end, edge' in the construct, አስግድ 'he made bow' (?); taken as a name only.
Name: ባሕረ is ባሕር 'sea' in the construct (?), then አስግድ as above; taken as a name.
Name: ግርማ 'majesty' as first element (?); taken as a name.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name with a transparent sense: ኵሉ 'all' + ለጽዮን 'for Zion'.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name with a transparent sense: ጽዮን 'Zion' + ሕግ 'law'.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
The famous pair of brothers of Aksum. አኀው 'brothers' (plural of አኅ) + ፍቁራን 'beloved ones' (plural of ፍቁር). ወ- 'and' joins the two names.
Name; spelling as printed.
Two names joined by ወ- 'and'; አኀው 'brothers' (plural of አኅ).
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
The Aksumite king Kaleb (Caleb).
Name with a transparent sense: ገብረ 'servant of' (construct) + መስቀል 'cross'. The same name as the Gebre Mesqel of the colophon proper (the king of Lalibela's time).
ቈስጠንጢኖስ is the Greek Constantine in Geʿez dress.
Name; በ- here is part of the name, not 'in' (?).
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelled with ሕ as printed.
Name; ዠ is the sign for ž (j), a sound added to the fidäl for foreign words.
Name; ሰገድ 'bowing' (from ሰገደ 'bow down').
Name with a transparent sense: ፍሬ 'fruit' + ሠናይ 'good'.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; spelling as printed.
ከላውድዮስ is the Greek Claudius in Geʿez dress.
Name: ግርማ 'majesty' (?) + አስፋ.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name: ሚካኤል is Michael.
Name; spelling as printed.
Name; a second Armah, spelled with ኅ as printed (the earlier one, unit 34, with ሐ).
Name: ሕዝበ is ሕዝብ 'people' in the construct; አናኒ is a name or word not analysed (?).
Name; spelling as printed.
አንበሳ 'lion' + ወ- 'and' + ወድም, a name or epithet not analysed (?); the Geʿez joins the two words with ወ.
Name: ድል 'victory' + ነአድ (Naod); the sense of the whole is not certain (?). The ፨ closes the list.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ተሀይደ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ለሕዝብ ፡ እለ ፡ ኢኮኑ ፡ እምነገደ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወሕዝበ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-after-him was-turned (?) kingdom to-people who not-are from-tribe-of David and-people-of Israel;
sentences.i: And after him the kingdom passed (?) to a people who were not of the tribe of David and the people of Israel;
sentences.n: ወእምድኅሬሁ 'and after him' (እምድኅረ + -ሁ). ተሀይደ is uncertain (?): 'was turned, passed' is a guess from ሀየደ 'go, depart'. ለሕዝብ 'to a people'; እለ ኢኮኑ 'who are not' (ኮነ negated). ነገድ 'tribe', ዳዊት David; the Zagwe are meant as not of the line of David and Solomon.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ አነ ፡ አቀንኦሙ ፡ በዘኢኮነ ፡ ሕዝብ ።
sentences.l: As said God: I I-will-make-them-jealous with-that-which-not-is people.
sentences.i: As God said: I will make them jealous with what is no people.
sentences.n: A quotation, rebuilt from the grammar: Deuteronomy 32:21, as the Geʿez has it. አቀንኦሙ is አቀነአ (causative of ቀነአ 'be jealous') 1cs imperfect with 3mp -ሙ 'them'; በዘ ኢኮነ ሕዝብ 'with that which is not a people'.

sentences.i: And after him he restored it to them;
sentences.n: አግብአ is the causative of ገብአ 'return': 'he gave back'; ሎሙ 'to them'. The subject and what is given back (the kingdom) are understood, not stated (?).
The first king of the restored line (c. 1270). ይኵኖ is a verb 'he has made' (ኰነ), አምላክ 'god, lord'; so 'May God make (it so)'-style, the sense of the name is not fixed (?).
